description: Search for files in a directory hierarchy.
The expression is built from operators, options, tests, and actions.

option.name: -amin
tip: File was last accessed less than, more than or exactly n minutes ago.

option.name: -and
tip: Logical AND; implied between two expressions with no operator in between.

option.name: -anewer
tip: Time of the last access of the current file is more recent than that of the last data modification of the reference file.

option.name: -atime
tip: File was last accessed less than, more than or exactly n*24 hours ago.
Fractional 24-hour periods are ignored, so -atime +1 matches a file accessed at least two days ago.

option.name: -cmin
tip: File's status was last changed less than, more than or exactly n minutes ago.

option.name: -cnewer
tip: Time of the last status change of the current file is more recent than that of the last data modification of the reference file.

option.name: -context
tip: (SELinux only) Security context of the file matches glob pattern.

option.name: -ctime
tip: File's status was last changed less than, more than or exactly n*24 hours ago.
Fractional 24-hour periods are ignored, so -ctime +1 matches a file whose status changed at least two days ago.

option.name: -D
tip: Print diagnostic information; this can help diagnose why find is not doing what you want.
The list of debug options should be comma separated.
Possible values: exec, opt, rates, search, stat, time, tree, all, help

next.name: all
tip: Enable all of the other debug options (but help).

next.name: exec
tip: Show diagnostic information relating to -exec, -execdir, -ok and -okdir.

next.name: help
tip: Explain the debugging options.

next.name: opt
tip: Prints diagnostic information relating to the optimisation of the expression tree.

next.name: rates
tip: Prints a summary indicating how often each predicate succeeded or failed.

next.name: search
tip: Navigate the directory tree verbosely.

next.name: stat
tip: Print messages as files are examined with the stat and lstat system calls.

next.name: time
tip: Show diagnostic information relating to time-of-day and timestamp comparisons.

next.name: tree
tip: Show the expression tree in its original and optimized form.

option.name: -daystart
tip: Measure times from the beginning of today rather than from 24 hours ago.
Affects only tests which appear later on the command line.

option.name: -delete
tip: Delete files or directories; true if removal succeeded.
Automatically turns on -depth, which makes -prune ineffective.

option.name: -depth
tip: Process each directory's contents before the directory itself.

option.name: -empty
tip: File is empty and is either a regular file or a directory.

option.name: -exec
tip: Execute command; true if 0 status is returned.
All following arguments are taken as arguments to the command until an argument consisting of ; is encountered.
The string {} is replaced by the current file name.

option.name: -execdir
tip: Like -exec, but the command is run from the subdirectory containing the matched file.
Much more secure than -exec, because it avoids race conditions while resolving the path.

option.name: -executable
tip: Matches files which are executable and directories which are searchable by the current user.

option.name: -false
tip: Always false.

option.name: -files0-from
tip: Read the starting points from file instead of getting them on the command line.
The starting points have to be separated by ASCII NUL characters.
Passing starting points this way and on the command line is mutually exclusive.

option.name: -fls
tip: True; like -ls, but write to file like -fprint.
The output file is always created, even if the predicate is never matched.

option.name: -follow
tip: Dereference symbolic links. Deprecated; use -L instead.
Affects only tests which appear after it on the command line.

option.name: -fprint
tip: True; print the full file name into file.
If file does not exist it is created; if it exists it is truncated.

option.name: -fprint0
tip: True; like -print0, but write to file like -fprint.

option.name: -fprintf
tip: True; like -printf, but write to file like -fprint.

option.name: -fstype
tip: File is on a filesystem of type type.
The valid types depend on the operating system.

option.name: -gid
tip: File's numeric group ID is less than, more than or exactly n.

option.name: -group
tip: File belongs to group gname (numeric group ID allowed).

option.name: -H
tip: Do not follow symbolic links, except while processing the command line arguments.

option.name: -ignore_readdir_race
tip: Do not emit an error message when a file disappears between the time its name is read and the time it is stat'ed.

option.name: -ilname
tip: Like -lname, but the match is case insensitive.
If -L or -follow is in effect, this test returns false unless the symbolic link is broken.

option.name: -iname
tip: Like -name, but the match is case insensitive.

option.name: -inum
tip: File has inode number smaller than, greater than or exactly n.
It is normally easier to use the -samefile test instead.

option.name: -iregex
tip: Like -regex, but the match is case insensitive.

option.name: -iwholename
tip: Like -path, but the match is case insensitive.
-iwholename is less portable than -ipath.

option.name: -L
tip: Follow symbolic links.
Implies -noleaf.

option.name: -links
tip: File has less than, more than or exactly n hard links.

option.name: -lname
tip: File is a symbolic link whose contents match shell pattern.
If -L or -follow is in effect, this test returns false unless the symbolic link is broken.

option.name: -ls
tip: True; list current file in ls -dils format on standard output.

option.name: -maxdepth
tip: Descend at most levels (a non-negative integer) levels of directories below the starting points.
-maxdepth 0 means only apply the tests and actions to the starting points themselves.

option.name: -mindepth
tip: Do not apply any tests or actions at levels less than levels (a non-negative integer).
-mindepth 1 means process all files except the starting points.

option.name: -mmin
tip: File's data was last modified less than, more than or exactly n minutes ago.

option.name: -mount
tip: Don't descend directories on other filesystems.

option.name: -mtime
tip: File's data was last modified less than, more than or exactly n*24 hours ago.
Fractional 24-hour periods are ignored, so -mtime +1 matches a file modified at least two days ago.

option.name: -name
tip: Base of file name (the path with the leading directories removed) matches shell pattern.
The pattern should not include a slash.
Enclose the pattern in quotes to protect it from expansion by the shell.

option.name: -newer
tip: Time of the last data modification of the current file is more recent than that of the last data modification of the reference file.

option.name: -newerXY
tip: Succeeds if timestamp X of the file being considered is newer than timestamp Y of the reference file.
X and Y can be a (access time), B (birth time), c (inode status change time), m (modification time) or t (the reference is interpreted directly as a time).
An invalid or unsupported combination is a fatal error.

option.name: -nogroup
tip: No group corresponds to file's numeric group ID.

option.name: -noignore_readdir_race
tip: Turns off the effect of -ignore_readdir_race.

option.name: -noleaf
tip: Do not optimize by assuming that directories contain 2 fewer subdirectories than their hard link count.
Needed on filesystems that do not follow the Unix directory-link convention, such as CD-ROM or MS-DOS filesystems.

option.name: -not
tip: Negate the following expression. Same as ! EXPR.

option.name: -nouser
tip: No user corresponds to file's numeric user ID.

option.name: -nowarn
tip: Turn warning messages off.

option.name: -O0
tip: Equivalent to optimisation level 1.

option.name: -O1
tip: The default optimisation level.
Expressions are reordered so that tests based only on the names of files are performed first.

option.name: -O2
tip: Any -type or -xtype tests are performed after tests based only on file names, but before tests that require information from the inode.

option.name: -O3
tip: The full cost-based query optimizer is enabled: cheap tests are performed first, and likely outcomes are tried first.

option.name: -ok
tip: Like -exec, but ask the user first.
If the command is run, its standard input is redirected from /dev/null.

option.name: -okdir
tip: Like -execdir, but ask the user first in the same way as for -ok.

option.name: -or
tip: Logical OR; expr2 is not evaluated if expr1 is true.

option.name: -P
tip: Never follow symbolic links (the default).

option.name: -perm
tip: File's permission bits are exactly mode (octal or symbolic).
Prefix the mode with - to require all of the bits to be set, or with / to require any of them.
The +mode form is no longer supported.

option.name: -print
tip: True; print the full file name on the standard output, followed by a newline.

option.name: -print0
tip: True; print the full file name followed by a null character instead of a newline.
Use this when the file names might contain newlines or other white space.

option.name: -printf
tip: True; print format on the standard output, interpreting backslash escapes and percent directives.
Unlike -print, -printf does not add a newline at the end of the string.

option.name: -prune
tip: True; do not descend into the current directory.

option.name: -quit
tip: Exit immediately, with return value zero if no errors have occurred.

option.name: -readable
tip: Matches files which are readable by the current user.

option.name: -regex
tip: File name matches regular expression pattern; this is a match on the whole path, not a search.
The regular expression dialect is Emacs by default and can be changed with -regextype.

option.name: -regextype
tip: Changes the regular expression syntax understood by -regex and -iregex tests which occur later on the command line.
Possible values: findutils-default, ed, emacs, gnu-awk, grep, posix-awk, awk, posix-basic, posix-egrep, egrep, posix-extended, posix-minimal-basic, sed

option.name: -samefile
tip: File refers to the same inode as name.

option.name: -size
tip: File uses less than, more than or exactly n units of space, rounding up.
Suffixes: b for 512-byte blocks (the default), c for bytes, w for two-byte words, k for KiB, M for MiB, G for GiB.

option.name: -true
tip: Always true.

option.name: -type
tip: File is of type c.
Several types can be supplied as a comma separated list (GNU extension).
Possible values: b, c, d, p, f, l, s, D

next.name: b
tip: Block (buffered) special.

next.name: c
tip: Character (unbuffered) special.

next.name: d
tip: Directory.

next.name: D
tip: Door (Solaris).

next.name: f
tip: Regular file.

next.name: l
tip: Symbolic link; never true under -L or -follow unless the link is broken.

next.name: p
tip: Named pipe (FIFO).

next.name: s
tip: Socket.

option.name: -uid
tip: File's numeric user ID is less than, more than or exactly n.

option.name: -used
tip: File was last accessed less than, more than or exactly n days after its status was last changed.

option.name: -user
tip: File is owned by user uname (numeric user ID allowed).

option.name: -warn
tip: Turn warning messages on.

option.name: -wholename
tip: File name matches shell pattern; the metacharacters do not treat / or . specially.
The match applies to the whole file name, starting from one of the start points.
-wholename is less portable than -path.

option.name: -writable
tip: Matches files which are writable by the current user.

option.name: -xtype
tip: The same as -type unless the file is a symbolic link; for links it checks the type of the file that -type does not check.
Several types can be supplied as a comma separated list.
Possible values: b, c, d, p, f, l, s

next.name: b
tip: Block (buffered) special.

next.name: c
tip: Character (unbuffered) special.

next.name: d
tip: Directory.

next.name: f
tip: Regular file.

next.name: l
tip: Symbolic link.

next.name: p
tip: Named pipe (FIFO).

next.name: s
tip: Socket.

global_option.name: --help
tip: Print a summary of the command-line usage of find and exit.

global_option.name: --version
tip: Print the find version number and exit.
